provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Whole numbers to one million
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the place value of digits in numbers up to one million
The pupils should be able to read and write numbers up to one million correctly
The pupils should be able to compare whole numbers up to one million

Introduction:
We have learned about smaller numbers in previous classes. Today we will extend our knowledge to work with numbers up to one million.

Content:
Place value is the value of each digit in a number. For example in 1 234 567, the 1 is in millions place. We use commas to separate thousands, millions etc. When comparing numbers, look at the highest place value first. If digits are the same, move to the next place value. For example 999 999 is less than 1 000 000 because 999 thousands is less than 1000 thousands.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in pairs to create place value charts using paper and write numbers up to one million.

Evaluation questions:
1. Write the number one million and twenty thousand in figures.
2. What is the place value of 5 in 456 789?
3. Which is bigger 899 999 or 900 000?

Summary:
Today we learned how to read, write and compare numbers up to one million using place value.

topics.title: Fractions review
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify equivalent fractions
The pupils should be able to add and subtract fractions with same denominators

Introduction:
We have learned about fractions in previous classes. Today we will review equivalent fractions and how to add and subtract them.

Content:
Equivalent fractions are fractions that look different but have the same value. For example 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6. To find equivalent fractions, multiply or divide both numerator and denominator by the same number. When adding or subtracting fractions with same denominators, we add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same. For example 1/3 + 2/3 = 3/3 = 1 whole.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to find equivalent fractions using fraction circles and fraction bars.

Evaluation questions:
1. Write two fractions equivalent to 3/4.
2. Add 2/5 + 1/5.
3. Subtract 3/4-1/4.

Summary:
Today we reviewed equivalent fractions and how to add and subtract fractions with the same denominator.

topics.title: Decimals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify the place value of decimal digits
The pupils should be able to add and subtract decimal numbers

Introduction:
We have learned about whole numbers and fractions. Today we will learn about decimal numbers which are another way to show parts of a whole.

Content:
Decimal numbers have a decimal point which separates whole numbers from decimal parts. The place values after the decimal point are tenths, hundredths, thousandths etc. For example in 3.45, 4 is in tenths place and 5 is in hundredths place. When adding or subtracting decimals, we line up the decimal points and add or subtract as usual. For example 2.3 + 1.25 = 3.55.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in pairs to add and subtract decimal amounts of money like Naira and Kobo.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the place value of 7 in 4.37?
2. Add 3.25 + 1.75.
3. Subtract 5.6-2.3.

Summary:
Today we learned about decimal place values and how to add and subtract decimal numbers.

topics.title: Multiplication
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to multiply numbers by two digit numbers
The pupils should be able to solve word problems involving multiplication

Introduction:
We have learned multiplication of numbers by one digit in previous classes. Today we will learn how to multiply by two digit numbers.

Content:
To multiply by two digit numbers, we use the long multiplication method. First multiply by the units digit, then multiply by the tens digit and add the results. For example 23 × 14: 23 × 4 = 92, then 23 × 10 = 230, then 92 + 230 = 322. In word problems, we look for key words like 'times', 'each', 'product' to know when to multiply.

Class activity:
Pupils will solve multiplication problems involving real life situations like calculating the total cost of multiple items at a market stall.

Evaluation questions:
1. Multiply 25 × 14.
2. Multiply 36 × 22.
3. A danfo bus carries 25 passengers. If it makes 8 trips in a day, how many passengers does it carry in total?

Summary:
Today we learned how to multiply by two digit numbers and solve multiplication word problems.

topics.title: Division
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform long division
The pupils should be able to solve word problems involving division

Introduction:
We have learned division in previous classes. Today we will learn long division which is used to divide by larger numbers.

Content:
Long division involves dividing step by step. For example 84 ÷ 12: 12 goes into 8 zero times, so we look at 84. 12 goes into 84 seven times (12 × 7 = 84), so the answer is 7. In word problems, we look for key words like 'share', 'divide', 'each', 'equal parts' to know when to divide.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to solve division problems involving sharing items equally among friends.

Evaluation questions:
1. Divide 96 ÷ 12.
2. Divide 120 ÷ 15.
3. A farmer has 84 oranges to share equally among 12 children. How many oranges will each child get?

Summary:
Today we learned how to perform long division and solve division word problems.

topics.title: Percentages
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to convert fractions to percentages
The pupils should be able to find simple percentages of amounts

Introduction:
We have learned about fractions and decimals. Today we will learn about percentages which are another way to express parts of a whole.

Content:
Percentage means per hundred. To convert a fraction to percentage, multiply by 100. For example 1/4 = 0.25 = 25%. To find a percentage of an amount, convert the percentage to a decimal or fraction and multiply. For example 20% of N500: 20% = 20/100 = 0.2, so 0.2 × 500 = N100.

Class activity:
Pupils will calculate discounts on items in a mock classroom shop.

Evaluation questions:
1. Convert 3/4 to percentage.
2. What is 50% of N200?
3. A kerosene stove was sold at 15% discount. If the original price was N800, what is the discount amount?

Summary:
Today we learned how to convert fractions to percentages and find simple percentages of amounts.

topics.title: Ratio and proportion
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write simple ratios
The pupils should be able to share quantities in a given ratio

Introduction:
We have learned about fractions and sharing. Today we will learn about ratios which help us compare quantities and share things in different proportions.

Content:
Ratio shows the relationship between quantities. For example the ratio of boys to girls in a class can be 3:2. To share in a ratio, add the parts of the ratio and divide the total by this sum. For example share N1000 in the ratio 3:2. Total parts = 3 + 2 = 5. Each part = 1000 ÷ 5 = N200. So first share = 3 × 200 = N600, second share = 2 × 200 = N400.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to share mock money in given ratios.

Evaluation questions:
1. Write the ratio of 4 apples to 6 oranges in simplest form.
2. Share N1200 in the ratio 3:2.
3. The ratio of boys to girls in a school is 5:4. If there are 360 boys, how many girls are there?

Summary:
Today we learned how to write simple ratios and share quantities in given ratios.

topics.title: Money
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to calculate profit and loss
The pupils should be able to solve shopping problems involving money

Introduction:
We have learned about numbers and operations. Today we will apply these concepts to money problems involving profit, loss and shopping.

Content:
Profit is when you sell something for more than you bought it. Loss is when you sell for less than you bought it. Profit or loss amount = selling price-cost price. Profit or loss percentage is calculated on the cost price. For example if you buy an item for N1000 and sell for N1200, profit = N200, profit percentage = (200/1000) × 100 = 20%.

Class activity:
Pupils will run a mock market stall where they buy and sell items and calculate profit or loss.

Evaluation questions:
1. A trader bought a bag of rice for N3000 and sold for N3600. What is the profit percentage?
2. A shoe was bought for N1500 and sold at a loss of 10%. What was the selling price?
3. If you buy 5 oranges at N200 and sell them at N250, what is your profit?

Summary:
Today we learned how to calculate profit and loss and solve shopping problems involving money.

topics.title: Length, weight, capacity
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to convert units of length, weight and capacity
The pupils should be able to solve real life measuring problems

Introduction:
We have learned about numbers. Today we will learn how to measure and convert different units of length, weight and capacity used in everyday life.

Content:
Common units of length are mm, cm, m, km. 1cm = 10mm, 1m = 100cm, 1km = 1000m. Common units of weight are g, kg. 1kg = 1000g. Common units of capacity are ml, l. 1l = 1000ml. To convert units, multiply or divide by the appropriate conversion factor. For example 2.5kg = 2.5 × 1000 = 2500g.

Class activity:
Pupils will measure objects in the classroom using rulers and weighing scales and convert between units.

Evaluation questions:
1. Convert 3.5kg to grams.
2. Convert 2500ml to liters.
3. A farmer harvested 2.5 tons of cassava. How many kilograms is this?

Summary:
Today we learned how to convert units of length, weight and capacity and solve real life measuring problems.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall and apply concepts learned this term
The pupils should be able to solve various types of mathematical problems

Introduction:
Today we will revise all the topics we have covered this term and assess your understanding through a class test.

Content:
We have covered whole numbers, fractions, decimals, multiplication, division, percentages, ratio and proportion, money, and measurement. Each topic has specific methods and formulas that we need to remember. For example when multiplying by two digit numbers we use long multiplication. When sharing in a ratio we add the parts first. When finding percentages we convert to decimal or fraction.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in teams to solve revision problems covering all topics of the term.

Evaluation questions:
1. Write 3/8 as a percentage.
2. Share N1500 in the ratio 3:2.
3. Multiply 45 × 23.
4. A trader bought 20 bags of rice at N2500 each and sold them at N3000 each. What is his profit percentage?

Summary:
Today we revised all topics covered this term and applied them to solve various problems.
